name: Rich McCormick
stance: Opposes a pause on advanced AI and a ban on superintelligence, prefers voluntary industry-led safety standards and existing law to new federal regulation, and frames AI policy as a race with China, while saying companies that slow down should not expect liability exemptions.

statements.text: Spoke at the AIxGlobal Risk Hill Forum on the opportunities and risks posed by AI.
Open-source AI is not a risk. Done right, it is one of our best defenses.
America cannot afford to pump the brakes while China is flooring it. If a CEO wants to slow down, that’s their choice. But don't expect exemptions from liability if your product causes harm.
The answer is not for Congress to rush in with sweeping new regulations that pick winners and losers, kill American innovation, and hand China an advantage.
Innovation and safety are not competing goals. America can — and must — lead on both.
Congress has already established AI guardrails. We don't need more Washington restrictions holding back American ingenuity.

Voluntary industry-led standards allow our leading AI companies room to innovate while holding themselves accountable for the technology they build. We cannot regulate our way to victory while China races ahead.
@nvidia's OpenShell is tackling AI safety the way America does best: by engineering solutions, not slowing innovation with more mandates from Washington.
As AI becomes more powerful, the answer isn’t to slow down American innovation. It’s to make sure security advances right alongside it.
There is a clear difference between AI tools acting with a customer’s permission and unauthorized access to financial accounts.
If you think America can afford to slow down on artificial intelligence, think again.
Democrats want to give China the biggest AI advantage of our lifetime. They are proposing a complete pause on advanced AI development and a ban on artificial superintelligence.
